dervis-irab:75-87.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بِمَواقِعِ النُّجُومِ): their places of falling and their places of setting; it was also said: their stations (manāzil); and it was also said: their dimming and scattering. Further explanation of it will come in the I'rab section.
(مُدْهِنُونَ): al-Rāghib said: "Idhān (compromising) is originally like tadhīn (anointing with oil), but it was made an expression for cajoling, being soft, and abandoning seriousness." Al-Muʾarrij said: the mudhin is the hypocrite, or the unbeliever who is gentle in his manner in order to conceal his unbelief; idhān and mudāhana are denial and hypocrisy, and its root is softness, and concealing the opposite of what one shows.

* I'rab:
(فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِمَواقِعِ النُّجُومِ): the fāʾ is resumptive and «لا» is redundant (zāʾida); the meaning is "So I swear". «لا» is added in oaths, so one says "لا والله" and "لا أفعل". Imruʾ al-Qays said:
لا وأبيك ابنة العامري ... لا يدعي القوم أني أفر
(No, by your father, O daughter of al-ʿĀmirī, the people shall not claim that I flee.)
The meaning is "by your father", and it was only added for emphasis and strengthening the speech. It was also said that it is negating, and the negated thing is omitted, namely the speech of the unbeliever and the denier, its implied form being "there is no truth in what the unbeliever says"; then He began anew and said "I swear". It was also said that it is the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ) entering a clause made of a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), namely "أنا أقسم", as when you say "لزيد منطلق"; then the mubtadaʾ was omitted and the lām became joined to its khabar, its implied form being "فلأقسم" with the lām alone. Abū Ḥayyān said: "The more likely view in my opinion is that it is a lām whose fatḥa was lengthened so that an alif was generated from it, as in his saying «أعوذ بالله من العقارب»." More of this discussion will come in our book. «أقسم» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنا"; «بمواقع النجوم» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أقسم».
(وَإِنَّهُ لَقَسَمٌ لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ): the wāw is parenthetical; «إنّ» and its noun, and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «قسم» is its khabar; «لو» is conditional; «تعلمون» is an imperfect verb, nominative; «عظيم» is a naʿt (adjective) of «قسم». The clause «لو تعلمون» is parenthetical between the qualified noun and its adjective, and the clause «إنه لقسم لو تعلمون عظيم» has no grammatical position because it is parenthetical between the oath and its answer; so they are two successive parentheses. The answer (jawāb) of «لو» is omitted, the implied form being "if you were people of knowledge you would know".
(إِنَّهُ لَقُرْآنٌ كَرِيمٌ): the clause is the answer of the oath and has no grammatical position; «إنّ» and its noun, and the shifted lām; «قرآن» is the khabar of «إنه» and «كريم» is a first adjective of «قرآن».
(فِي كِتابٍ مَكْنُونٍ): «في كتاب» is a second adjective of «قرآن», and «مكنون» is an adjective of «كتاب».
(لا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ): «لا» is negating; «يمسّه» is an imperfect verb with its object; «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); «المطهرون» is the fāʿil of «يمسّه», and the clause is a third adjective of «قرآن». It was also said that «لا» is prohibitive and «يمسّه» is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by «لا», but since it was assimilated (idghām) its final letter was given a vowel because of the assimilation, and the vowel was a ḍamma in harmony with the hāʾ. There is no need for this contrivance; what we have mentioned is preferable and more consistent with the harmony of the adjectives. What we have adopted is supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd «ما يمسّه» with the negating «ما». In "touching it" there is a metonymy (kināya) for what it entails, namely the negation of access to it and to what it contains.
(تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ): a fourth adjective, and «من رب العالمين» is an adjective of «تنزيل».
(أَفَبِهذَا الْحَدِيثِ أَنْتُمْ مُدْهِنُونَ): the hamza is for the rebuking, disapproving interrogative; the fāʾ is a conjunction; «بهذا» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «مدهنون»; «الحديث» is a badal (substitute) for the demonstrative; «أنتم» is a mubtadaʾ and «مدهنون» is the khabar.
(وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; «تجعلون» is an imperfect verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; «رزقكم» is the first object of «تجعلون»; «أنّ» and its noun, and the clause «تكذبون» is its khabar; «أنّ» with what falls within its scope is in the position of the second object. A muḍāf must be implied, i.e. "the thanks for your provision".
(فَلَوْلا إِذا بَلَغَتِ الْحُلْقُومَ): the fāʾ is resumptive; «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) meaning "هلّا", and nothing but a verb comes after it, so the implied form is "فلولا ترجعونها إذا بلغت الحلقوم"; thus the governor of «إذا» is the verb occurring after «لولا», namely «ترجعونها». «بلغت» is a past verb and its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "النفس", i.e. when the soul reaches the throat at death.
(وَأَنْتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنْظُرُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «أنتم» is a mubtadaʾ; «حين» is an adverb annexed to one like it, namely «إذ», and the tanwīn in it is a substitute for the clause annexed to it, i.e. "when the soul reaches the throat"; the clause «تنظرون» is the khabar of «أنتم», and the clause «وأنتم حينئذ تنظرون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of «بلغت».
(وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْكُمْ وَلكِنْ لا تُبْصِرُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial; «نحن» is a mubtadaʾ and «أقرب» the khabar; «إليه» and «منكم» are attached to «أقرب»; the wāw is a conjunction; «لكن» is lightened and inoperative (muhmala), for rectification (istidrāk); «لا» is negating; «تبصرون» is an imperfect verb, nominative, from baṣīra, i.e. knowledge.
(فَلَوْلا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ تَرْجِعُونَها إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; «لولا» is a particle of urging reinforcing the first «لولا»; «إن» is conditional; «كنتم» is «كان» and its noun; «غير مدينين» is the khabar, i.e. not to be requited by being resurrected, i.e. not to be resurrected. «ترجعونها» is the governor of «إذا»; the adverb was placed before its governor, to which the two conditions are attached, namely «إن كنتم غير مدينين» and «إن كنتم غير صادقين» [Translator's note: the Quranic text reads «إن كنتم صادقين»; the wording "غير صادقين" is as in the source]. The meaning of their being attached to it is that it is the requital of both of them, i.e. of each one of them; so there is an inversion in the speech, and the meaning is: why do you not return it, if you deny the resurrection and are truthful in denying it? The summary of the speech: if you are truthful in denying the resurrection, then return the soul of the dying person to his body so that death is removed from him, and thus resurrection is removed.

* Rhetoric:
The implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya) in His saying «فإذا بلغت الحلقوم» [Translator's note: the Quranic text reads «فلولا إذا بلغت الحلقوم»; quoted as in the source]: it is as if the soul were a bodily thing that reaches the throat in a perceptible movement.

dervis-irab:88-96.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَرَوْحٌ وَرَيْحانٌ): rawḥ, with fatḥa, is rest, mercy and the breeze of the wind; rayḥān is mercy and provision, as in al-Mukhtār. In al-Qāmūs: "Rayḥān is a sweet-smelling plant, or every plant like that, or its tips or its leaves; and a child; and provision."
(تَصْلِيَةُ): burning.

* I'rab:
(فَأَمَّا إِنْ كانَ مِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ): resumptive speech, set forth to begin explaining the state of the deceased after death, following the explanation of his state at the time of death. «أمّا» is a particle of condition and detailing; «إن» is conditional; «كان» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb and its noun is latent (mustatir), i.e. the deceased; «من المقربين» is the khabar (predicate) of «كان».
(فَرَوْحٌ وَرَيْحانٌ وَجَنَّةُ نَعِيمٍ): the fāʾ links the answer of «أمّا», and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of «إن» is omitted because what is mentioned indicates it; omitting the answer of «إن» is very common. «روح» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is omitted and placed before it, i.e. "فله روح", and what follows is conjoined to it.
(وَأَمَّا إِنْ كانَ مِنْ أَصْحابِ الْيَمِينِ فَسَلامٌ لَكَ مِنْ أَصْحابِ الْيَمِينِ): conjoined to what preceded and equal to it in its i'rab. «سلام» is a mubtadaʾ because of the meaning of supplication in it; «لك» is the khabar of «سلام»; «من أصحاب اليمين» is a naʿt (adjective) or a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَأَمَّا إِنْ كانَ مِنَ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ الضَّالِّينَ): conjoined to the clause «فأما إن كان», and the i'rab is the same, so renew your acquaintance with it.
(فَنُزُلٌ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ وَتَصْلِيَةُ جَحِيمٍ): the fāʾ links the answer of «أمّا»; «نزل» is a mubtadaʾ whose fronted khabar is omitted; «من حميم» is an adjective of «نزل»; «تصلية جحيم» is conjoined to «نزل».
(إِنَّ هذا لَهُوَ حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ): «إنّ» and its noun, and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; «حق اليقين» is the khabar of «إنّ» or the khabar of «هو», and the nominal clause is the khabar of «إنّ». The annexation of «حق» to «اليقين» is an annexation of the qualified noun to its adjective.
(فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ): its i'rab has preceded, and we repeat it in order to add some benefits to it. «فسبّح» is an imperative verb meaning "declare transcendent"; the word «اسم» is redundant (zāʾid), i.e. declare your Lord the Magnificent transcendent. It is also permissible that the bāʾ be for the ḥāl, i.e. so glorify while engaged with the name of your Lord, or seeking blessing by it; and it is permissible that the bāʾ be for transitivity, on the basis that «سبّح» is sometimes transitive by itself and at other times by a preposition.

dervis-irab:1-16.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْواقِعَةُ): the Resurrection; it is described as something that will inevitably befall (taqaʿ), or as though it were befalling in itself.
(بُسَّتِ): crumbled. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "basastu al-ḥinṭa wa-ghayrahā bassan, of the pattern qatala, which is crumbling; so it is basīsa, of the pattern faʿīla in the sense of mafʿūla (passive)."
(هَباءً): al-habāʾ is dust like a ray of light in its fineness; it often comes out with the sun's ray through a window that lets it in.
(مُنْبَثًّا): spread about, scattered of itself, without need of air to scatter it.
(أَصْحابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ): those who are given their records in their right hands; from al-yumn, blessing.
(أَصْحابُ الْمَشْئَمَةِ): those who are given their records in their left hands, the ill-omened (al-mashāʾīm) for their own selves.
(ثُلَّةٌ): a group.
(مَوْضُونَةٍ): woven, interlaced, like the description of a coat of mail. Al-Aʿshā said:
ومن نسج داود موضونة ... تساق إلى الحيّ عيرا فعيرا
(And closely woven [mail] of David's weaving, driven to the tribe caravan after caravan.)

* I'rab:
(إِذا وَقَعَتِ الْواقِعَةُ): regarding (إذا) there are several views:
1- It is a pure adverb (ẓarf) with no conditional meaning, governed by the meaning of negation in (ليس), as though it were said: "denial of its occurrence is negated when it occurs." Al-Zamakhsharī took this view and said: "If you say: by what is (إذا) put in the accusative? I say: by (ليس), as in your saying 'On Friday I have no occupation (yawma al-jumuʿati laysa lī shughl)'." Abū Ḥayyān rejected it, saying: "As for putting it in the accusative by (ليس), no grammarian, nor anyone who has acquired anything of the craft of i'rab, would go to the like of this. For (ليس) in negation is like (ما) and (لا), which do not govern [an adverb], and so likewise (ليس). That is because (ليس) is stripped of the indication of event and time, and saying that it is a verb is by way of figurative usage, since the definition of a verb does not apply to it. What governs an adverb is only the event that occurs in it: if you say 'On Friday I will stand', the standing occurs on Friday; but (ليس) has no event, so how can it govern an adverb? The example he compared it to — 'On Friday I have no occupation' — does not show that 'Friday' is accusative by (ليس); rather it is accusative by what governs the predicate of (ليس), namely the preposition and its genitive noun. So it is a case of fronting the predicate before (ليس), and fronting that is based on the permissibility of fronting the predicate of (ليس) before it, which is disputed; and 'qāʾiman laysa Zayd' (standing, Zayd is not) has not been heard from the tongue of the Arabs. (ليس) indicates only the predicative judgement about the subject of the judgement, so it is like (ما); but because nominative pronouns attach to it, some people made it a verb, while in reality it is a particle of negation like the negating (ما). It appears from al-Zamakhsharī's likening of (إذا) to his saying 'yawma al-jumuʿa' that he stripped it of the conditional indication that is predominant in it. Were it a condition with the apodosis being the clause headed by (ليس), the fāʾ would be required, unless it is dropped in poetry, where that has occurred. So you say: 'idhā aḥsana ilayka Zaydun fa-lasta tatruku mukāfaʾatahu' (if Zayd does you good, you will not fail to repay him), and 'lasta' without the fāʾ is not permissible, unless one is compelled to it."
2- That what governs it is an implied "udhkur" (remember).
3- That it is conditional and its apodosis (jawāb) is implied, i.e. "when the Event befalls, such-and-such will be", and that is what governs it.
4- That it is conditional and governed by the verb after it which follows it directly. This is the choice of Abū Ḥayyān, who followed Makkī in it. Makkī said: "What governs it is (وقعت), because it may be used for conditional requital, so the verb after it governs it, just as [the verb after them] governs the conditional (ما) and (من) in your saying 'mā tafʿal afʿal' (whatever you do, I will do) and 'man tukrim ukrim' (whomever you honour, I will honour)."
5- That it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (إذا رجت) its khabar (predicate); this is on the view that it is declinable (mutaṣarrifa).
6- That it is an adverb of (خافضة رافعة), as Abū al-Baqāʾ said, i.e. when it befalls it will lower and raise.
7- That it is an adverb of (رجت), and the second (إذا) is either a badal (substitute) of the first or a repetition of it.
8- That what governs it is what is indicated by His words (فأصحاب الميمنة), i.e. when it befalls, the states of people in it will become clear.
9- That the apodosis is His words (فأصحاب الميمنة).
10- Al-Jurjānī said: (إذا) is redundant (ṣila), i.e. "the Event has befallen", like (اقتربت الساعة) and (أتى أمر الله); it is as one says "the fast has come", i.e. drawn near and approached.
(وقعت الواقعة) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent).
(لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِها كاذِبَةٌ): (ليس) is a past verb, rigid (jāmid) and incomplete (nāqiṣ); (لوقعتها) is its fronted predicate, and the lām means "fī" (in), with a muḍāf implied, i.e. "there is no lying [soul] to be found at the time of its occurrence"; (كاذبة) is the noun of (ليس). (كاذبة) is an adjective of an omitted qualified noun, i.e. "a lying soul". It is also said that (كاذبة) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that came in the form of an active participle, meaning "lying".
(خافِضَةٌ رافِعَةٌ): (خافضة) is the predicate of an omitted subject, and (رافعة) a second predicate.
(إِذا رُجَّتِ الْأَرْضُ رَجًّا): (إذا) may be a badal of the first (إذا), or a tawkīd (emphasis) of it, or its predicate on the view that it is a subject — this has preceded in detail. It may also be conditional, governed either by something implied or by its verb that follows it, as preceded for its counterpart. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: "It may be put in the accusative by (خافضة رافعة), i.e. it lowers and raises at the time of the shaking of the earth and the crumbling of the mountains, because at that time what is high is lowered and what is low is raised." (رجّا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
(وَبُسَّتِ الْجِبالُ بَسًّا): the clause is conjoined to the preceding clause.
(فَكانَتْ هَباءً مُنْبَثًّا): the fāʾ is conjunctive; (كانت) is an incomplete past verb, its noun latent (mustatir), its implied form being "hiya" (it); (هباء) is its predicate, and (منبثّا) an adjective of (هباء).
(وَكُنْتُمْ أَزْواجاً ثَلاثَةً): conjoined to (رجّت); (كان), its noun and its predicate; (ثلاثة) is a naʿt (adjective) of (أزواجا).
(فَأَصْحابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ ما أَصْحابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ): the fāʾ is conjunctive, of ramification (tafrīʿiyya), beginning the detailing and explanation of the states of the three kinds. (أصحاب الميمنة) is a subject; (ما) is interrogative, in the position of the nominative as a second subject, and what is intended by the interrogative is magnification; the second (أصحاب الميمنة) is the predicate of (ما), and the clause is the predicate of the first subject. Repeating the subject here with its own wording made a linking element — the pronoun — unnecessary. Its like is (الحاقة ما الحاقة) and (القارعة ما القارعة), and it occurs only in contexts of magnification or belittling. This is the first category of the kinds.
(وَأَصْحابُ الْمَشْئَمَةِ ما أَصْحابُ الْمَشْئَمَةِ): conjoined to what preceded; what is intended here is belittling their standing. They are the second category of the kinds.
(وَالسَّابِقُونَ السَّابِقُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive; (السابقون) is a subject and the [second] (السابقون) a tawkīd. They are the third category of the kinds, and the most deeply rooted in merit.
(أُولئِكَ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ): (أولئك) is a subject and (المقربون) its predicate, and the clause is the predicate of (السابقون); the demonstrative made the linking element — the pronoun — unnecessary. Al-Zamakhsharī chose that the [second] (السابقون) be a predicate and not a tawkīd. He said: "And the forerunners are those whose state you know and whose description has reached you, like his saying 'and ʿAbd Allāh is ʿAbd Allāh', and the saying of Abū al-Najm 'and my poetry is my poetry', as though he said: and my poetry is what has reached you and whose eloquence you have heard of. [The second] (السابقون) has been made a tawkīd and (أولئك المقربون) the predicate, but that is not [convincing]." This is what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned, and it is not far-fetched; rather it is perhaps more firmly grounded in eloquence. Do you not see how the setting forth of the state of the forerunners came first through His words (أولئك المقربون), combining the demonstrative, pointing to something known, with the predication about it by His words (المقربون), made definite by the alif and lām of prior reference (al-ʿahdiyya)? Below we quote the text of what Abū Ḥayyān presented. He said: "(والسابقون السابقون): they allowed it to be a subject and predicate, like their saying 'anta anta' (you are you), and his saying 'I am Abū al-Najm and my poetry is my poetry', i.e. those who reached the utmost in forerunning — i.e. in acts of obedience — and excelled in them, and whose state is known; and [they allowed] the [second] (السابقون) to be a verbal tawkīd, with 'al-khayr' in what follows that." [Translator's note: so in the source, «والخير»; evidently «والخبر» (the predicate) is in what follows.] Abū al-Baqāʾ's wording: "The words of the Exalted (والسابقون): the first is a subject and the second its predicate, i.e. those who are foremost in good are those foremost to Paradise. It is also said that the second is an adjective of the first, or repeated as emphasis, and the predicate is (أولئك)."
(فِي جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ): a second predicate, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in (المقربون), or attached to it, i.e. they have been brought near to Allah's mercy in the Gardens of Bliss. The annexation of "gardens" to "bliss" is annexation of a place to what is in it, as one says "the house of hospitality", "the house of the call" and "the house of justice".
(ثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ وَقَلِيلٌ مِنَ الْآخِرِينَ): (ثلّة) is the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e. "they are a large group of the earlier ones"; (من الأولين) is an adjective; (قليل) is conjoined to (ثلّة); and (من الآخرين) is an adjective of (قليل). Al-Jalāl [al-Maḥallī] chose that (ثلّة) be nominative as a subject because it is qualified, with its predicate being the following (على سرر).
(عَلى سُرُرٍ مَوْضُونَةٍ): either a predicate, on the view that (ثلّة) is a subject, or a second adjective of (ثلّة), on the view that it is the predicate of an implied subject.
(مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَيْها مُتَقابِلِينَ): two ḥāls of the pronoun in (عليها), i.e. they are settled upon them, reclining, facing one another, not one of them looking at another. [Translator's note: so in the source, «لا ينظر بعضهم إلى بعض»; the commonly cited gloss is "none of them looks at the back of another" (إلى قفا بعض), and the phrase may be defective here.]

dervis-irab:17-26.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُخَلَّدُونَ): remaining forever; they do not die, grow old or change. It is also said to be from al-khuld, which is the earring. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
وهل ينعمن إلا سعيد مخلد ... قليل الهموم ما يبيت بأوجال
(Does anyone enjoy life but a fortunate, ever-young one, of few cares, who does not pass the night in fears?)
Al-wildān is the plural of walīd — like ṣibyān — meaning "born one" (mawlūd); walad is pluralised as awlād.
(مَعِينٍ): wine flowing from a source that neither overflows nor ever ceases.
(لا يُصَدَّعُونَ): no headache (ṣudāʿ) befalls them because of it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its literal sense is that their headache does not issue from it." Al-ṣudāʿ is the well-known ailment that afflicts a person in his head; and wine has an effect [on it]. ʿAlqama said, describing wine:
تشفي الصداع ولا يؤذيك صالبها ... ولا يخالطها في الرأس تدويم
(It cures the headache, its fever does not harm you, and no dizziness mingles with it in the head.)
(يُنْزِفُونَ): with fatḥa or kasra on the zāy, from "nuzifa al-shārib" and "anzafa". One says "nuzifa al-rajul", in the passive, i.e. his mind went from intoxication; and "nuzifa al-rajulu daman": he had a nosebleed and all his blood came out. Both are attested.

* I'rab:
(يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ): the clause is resumptive, and it may also be circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (عليهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يطوف); (ولدان) is the fāʿil (agent); (مخلدون) is a naʿt (adjective) of (ولدان). The meaning is: boys circulate around them for service, who do not grow old or change; rather their form is always the form of youths.
(بِأَكْوابٍ وَأَبارِيقَ وَكَأْسٍ مِنْ مَعِينٍ): (بأكواب) is attached to (يطوف), and what follows it is conjoined to it; (من معين) is an adjective of (كأس).
(لا يُصَدَّعُونَ عَنْها وَلا يُنْزِفُونَ): the clause is resumptive, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in (عليهم). (لا) is negating; (يصدعون) is in the passive, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (عنها) is attached to it; (ولا ينزفون) is conjoined to (لا يصدعون).
(وَفاكِهَةٍ مِمَّا يَتَخَيَّرُونَ): conjoined to what preceded, i.e. to (كأس); (مما) is an adjective of (فاكهة), and the clause (يتخيرون) is the ṣila (relative clause).
(وَلَحْمِ طَيْرٍ مِمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ): also conjoined to what preceded.
(وَحُورٌ عِينٌ): it is read in the nominative, and there are several views on it. First, it is conjoined to (ولدان), i.e. they circulate among them for enjoyment, not for service. Second, it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "they have ḥūr", or "and there are ḥūr". Third, it is the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e. "and their women are ḥūr". It is also read in the accusative, by implying "they are given ḥūr" or "they are rewarded with ḥūr". It is also read in the genitive, conjoined to (أكواب) in form but not in meaning, because the ḥūr are not passed around; and it is said to be conjoined to (جنات), i.e. "in gardens and among ḥūr". (عين) is an adjective of (حور).
(كَأَمْثالِ اللُّؤْلُؤِ الْمَكْنُونِ): (كأمثال) is a second adjective of (حور); (اللؤلؤ) is a muḍāf ilayhi (second term of the genitive construct), and (المكنون) an adjective.
(جَزاءً بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): (جزاء) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. all that is done for them as a recompense; or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "We recompensed them with a recompense". (بما) is attached to (جزاء); the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila; (كان) and its noun, and the clause (يعملون) is its predicate.
(لا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيها لَغْواً وَلا تَأْثِيماً): (لا) is negating; (يسمعون) is an imperfect verb and the wāw its agent; (فيها) is attached to (يسمعون); (لغوا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the wāw is a conjunction, (لا) is negating, and (تأثيما) is conjoined to (لغوا), i.e. obscene speech or what incurs sin.
(إِلَّا قِيلًا سَلاماً سَلاماً): (إلا) is a particle of exception, and the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ); (قيلا) is excepted in a disconnected exception, necessarily accusative. Regarding (سلاما سلاما) there are several views. First, it is a badal (substitute) of (قيلا), i.e. they hear in it nothing but "peace, peace". Second, it is an adjective of (قيلا). Third, it is accusative by (قيلا), since it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. except that they say "peace, peace"; al-Zajjāj chose this. Fourth, that it is an absolute object of an omitted verb, i.e. "they greeted with peace".

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words (كأمثال اللؤلؤ المكنون) there is a mursal mujmal simile (tashbīh mursal mujmal); the point of similarity, which is being guarded, is omitted. The poet said, describing a woman as guarded and not exposed, likening her to a pearl concealed in its shell:
قامت تراءى بين سجفي كلة ... كالشمس يوم طلوعها بالأسعد أو درّة صدفية غوّاصها ... بهج متى يرها يهلّ ويسجد
(She rose, showing herself between the two curtains of a canopy, like the sun on the day it rises with the luckiest stars; or a pearl of the shell whose diver is overjoyed — whenever he sees it, he cries out and bows down.)
2- In His words (لا يصدعون عنها ولا ينزفون) there is the device of concision (ijāz), which has preceded: in these two words He gathered all the defects of wine in this world.

dervis-irab:27-40.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سِدْرٍ): al-sidr is the lote tree (nabq).
(مَخْضُودٍ): the root meaning of al-khaḍd is bending a soft stick; hence al-makhḍūd is that which has no thorns, because what is moist and soft mostly has no thorns. In al-Mukhtār: "khaḍada al-shajar: he cut off its thorns; its pattern is that of ḍaraba; so it is khaḍīd and makhḍūd." Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt said, describing Paradise:
إن الحدائق في الجنان ظليلة ... فيها الكواعب سدرها مخضود
(The orchards in the Gardens are shady; in them are full-breasted maidens, and their lote trees are thornless.)
(طَلْحٍ): al-ṭalḥ is the banana tree. Abū ʿUbayda said: it is every large tree with many thorns. One of the camel-drivers chanting to his camels said:
بشرها دليلها وقالا ... غدا ترين الطلح والجبلا
(Her guide gave her good tidings and said: tomorrow you will see the ṭalḥ trees and the mountains.)
Al-Zajjāj said: al-ṭalḥ is the umm ghaylān (acacia) tree, so it may be in the finest state.
(مَنْضُودٍ): a passive participle from "naḍadtu al-matāʿ", i.e. I placed the goods one on top of another.
(أَبْكاراً): al-bikr is the woman whom no man has deflowered, so she is in her first created state, as when she was brought into being. From it comes al-bukra for the beginning of the day, al-bākūra for the first fruit, and al-bakr, the young camel, whose plural is bikār and bikāra; and "the people came ʿalā bakratihim" and "ʿalā bakrati abīhim" (all together, to the last one).
(عُرُباً): plural of ʿarūb, the woman who shows affection to her husband out of passionate love for him.
(أَتْراباً): plural of tirb, which is "al-ladhdha" [Translator's note: so in the source, «اللذة»; evidently «اللِّدة» (the peer of the same age)] who grows up with his like in childhood. It is taken from the child's playing with dust (turāb), i.e. they are like children who are of the same age. ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
أبرزوها مثل المهاة تهادى ... بين عشر كواعب أتراب
(They brought her out like a wild cow, swaying gently among ten full-breasted maidens of equal age.)

* I'rab:
(وَأَصْحابُ الْيَمِينِ ما أَصْحابُ الْيَمِينِ): resumptive speech, set forth to begin detailing what was first stated in summary. (أصحاب) is the mubtadaʾ (subject); (ما) is an interrogative noun for magnification, in the position of the nominative as a subject; (أصحاب اليمين) is the khabar (predicate) of (ما), and the clause is the predicate of (أصحاب). The linking element is the repetition of the subject in its own wording, as preceded.
(فِي سِدْرٍ مَخْضُودٍ وَطَلْحٍ مَنْضُودٍ): a second predicate of (أصحاب), or the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e. "they are among lote trees"; (مخضود) is a naʿt (adjective) of (سدر).
(وَظِلٍّ مَمْدُودٍ وَماءٍ مَسْكُوبٍ وَفاكِهَةٍ كَثِيرَةٍ لا مَقْطُوعَةٍ وَلا مَمْنُوعَةٍ وَفُرُشٍ مَرْفُوعَةٍ): conjoined to "wa-lahu fī sidr" [Translator's note: so in the source, «عطف على وله في سدر»; evidently for «عطف على قوله في سدر», i.e. conjoined to His words (في سدر)]. (لا) in (لا مقطوعة) is for negation, as in your saying "I passed by a man neither tall nor short"; that is why its repetition is required.
(إِنَّا أَنْشَأْناهُنَّ إِنْشاءً): inna and its noun; the clause (أنشأناهنّ) is the predicate; (إنشاء) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The wording of al-Kashshāf: "(إنّا أنشأناهنّ إنشاء): We began their creation anew, without birth. Either those whose creation was originated are meant, or those whose creation was renewed. It is reported from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that Umm Salama asked him about the words of the Exalted (إنّا أنشأناهنّ إنشاء), and he said: 'O Umm Salama, they are the ones who were taken in the abode of this world as old women, grey-haired and bleary-eyed; Allah made them, after old age, of equal age, born at one time in [their] evenness; whenever their husbands come to them, they find them virgins.' When ʿĀʾisha heard that from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, she said: 'Oh, the pain!' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'There is no pain there.'"
(فَجَعَلْناهُنَّ أَبْكاراً عُرُباً أَتْراباً): the fāʾ is conjunctive; (جعلناهنّ) is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (أبكارا) is the second direct object; (عربا) and (أترابا) are two adjectives of (أبكارا).
(لِأَصْحابِ الْيَمِينِ): (لأصحاب اليمين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أنشأناهنّ).
(ثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ وَثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْآخِرِينَ): (ثلّة) is the predicate of an omitted subject; (من الأولين) is an adjective of (ثلّة); and (ثلّة من الآخرين) is conjoined to what preceded.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words (وفرش مرفوعة): if (الفرش) is explained as the plural of firāsh (bed), its meaning is literal, i.e. raised upon couches. If women are meant by it, it is an allusion (kināya) to a described entity; the Arabs call a woman "firāsh" (bed) and "libās" (garment). This interpretation is indicated by His words (إنّا أنشأناهنّ إنشاء).
2- In His words (عربا أترابا) there is also an allusion to their returning to, or being brought into being at, a young age. An old woman said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Pray to Allah to admit me into Paradise." He said: "Old women do not enter Paradise." She turned away weeping, and he, upon him be blessings and peace, said: "Tell her that she will not be an old woman." Also from him ﷺ: "The people of Paradise will enter Paradise hairless of body, beardless, white, curly-haired, with kohl on their eyes, aged thirty-three." Al-ʿurub is the plural of ʿarūb, the woman who shows affection to her husband. Al-Mubarrad said: she is the one passionately in love with her husband. Zayd ibn Aslam said: she is the one of fine speech. Al-atrāb are those born at one time, of a single age.

dervis-irab:41-56.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سَمُومٍ): al-samūm is the hot wind that enters the pores (masāmm) of the body; the pores of the body are its openings. From it is taken al-samm (poison), which enters through the pores.
(يَحْمُومٍ): al-yaḥmūm is jet-black smoke. In al-Mukhtār: "ḥammamahu taḥmīman: he blackened his face with charcoal. Al-ḥumam is ashes and charcoal, and everything burnt by fire, the singular being ḥumama. Al-yaḥmūm is smoke."
(الْحِنْثِ): sin. Al-ḥinth is also used to express reaching puberty; from it is their saying "they had not reached al-ḥinth". That was said only because a person, on reaching puberty, is held to account for al-ḥinth, i.e. sin. "Taḥannatha fulān" means he avoided sin. In the ḥadīth: "He ﷺ used to taḥannath in the fire of Ḥirāʾ" [Translator's note: so in the source, «بنار حراء»; evidently «بغار حراء» (in the cave of Ḥirāʾ)], i.e. he devoted himself to worship, avoiding sin. So the pattern tafaʿʿala in all these is for privation (salb).
(الْهِيمِ): thirsty camels that are not quenched by water because of a disease that afflicts them; the singular is ahyam and the feminine haymāʾ. The origin of hīm is "huym", with ḍamma on the hāʾ, on the pattern of ḥumr, but the ḍamma was changed to a kasra to suit the yāʾ. The wording of al-Samīn: "Al-hīm is the plural of ahyam and haymāʾ, which are the male and female camel afflicted by al-huyām, a disease causing thirst from which the camels drink until they die or fall gravely ill."

* I'rab:
(وَأَصْحابُ الشِّمالِ ما أَصْحابُ الشِّمالِ): the i'rab of its parallel has preceded shortly before, so refresh your memory of it. The speech is resumptive, set forth to begin detailing what He stated in summary of their states, after He detailed the state of the Companions of the Right.
(فِي سَمُومٍ وَحَمِيمٍ): a second khabar (predicate), or the predicate of an implied subject; its parallel has preceded.
(وَظِلٍّ مِنْ يَحْمُومٍ لا بارِدٍ وَلا كَرِيمٍ): conjoined to what preceded.
(إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا قَبْلَ ذلِكَ مُتْرَفِينَ): the clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya) and has no grammatical position. Inna and its noun, and the clause (كانوا) is its predicate; (كان) and its noun; the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) or to (مترفين); and (مترفين) is the predicate of (كانوا).
(وَكانُوا يُصِرُّونَ عَلَى الْحِنْثِ الْعَظِيمِ): conjoined to what preceded; (كان) and its noun, and the clause (يصرّون) is its predicate; (على الحنث) is attached to (يصرّون), and (العظيم) is a naʿt (adjective).
(وَكانُوا يَقُولُونَ أَإِذا مِتْنا وَكُنَّا تُراباً وَعِظاماً أَإِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ): also conjoined; (كان) and its noun, and the clause (يقولون) is its predicate. The hamza is interrogative; (إذا) is an adverb of condition attached to something indicated by His words (أإنا لمبعوثون). Do you not see that (إذا) is an adverb of time, so it must have a verb or the meaning of a verb to which it is attached? It cannot be attached to (متنا), because that is its muḍāf ilayhi (second term of the genitive construct), and the second term of a construct does not govern the first. And since it cannot be referred to this verb, nor to what comes after (إنّ) — inasmuch as what comes after (إنّ) does not govern what precedes it, just as what comes after (لا) does not govern what precedes it, so likewise what comes after the interrogative cannot govern what precedes it — you know that it is attached to something indicated by His words (أإنا لمبعوثون), namely "we will be gathered" or "we will be raised", and the like of what this speech indicates.
(متنا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (كنّا) is conjoined to (متنا); (كان) and its noun, and (ترابا) its predicate; (عظاما) is conjoined to (ترابا). The hamza is interrogative; inna and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and (مبعوثون) its predicate.
(أَوَآباؤُنَا الْأَوَّلُونَ): the hamza is interrogative; the wāw is a conjunction; (آباؤنا) is conjoined to the latent (mustakinn) pronoun in (مبعوثون). Conjoining to the pronoun without the emphasising "naḥnu" is acceptable because of the separator, namely the hamza. It is also said that what it is conjoined to is the position of (إنّ) and its noun, taking into account that the conjoined word precedes the predicate, the implied form being "Shall we, or our fathers, be raised?" (الأولون) is an adjective of (آباؤنا).
(قُلْ إِنَّ الْأَوَّلِينَ وَالْآخِرِينَ لَمَجْمُوعُونَ إِلى مِيقاتِ يَوْمٍ مَعْلُومٍ): resumptive speech, set forth to refute their denial and to establish the truth. Inna and its noun; (الآخرين) is conjoined to (الأولين); the shifted lām; (مجموعون) is the predicate of (إنّ); (إنّ), its noun and its predicate are in the position of the accusative as the speech quoted (maqūl al-qawl). (إلى ميقات يوم) is attached to (مجموعون), and (معلوم) is an adjective of (يوم). "Gathering" has been made to include the meaning of "driving", and so it was made transitive with (إلى); otherwise, the apparent [construction] would be to make it transitive with (في).
(ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ أَيُّهَا الضَّالُّونَ الْمُكَذِّبُونَ): (ثم) is a conjunction for sequence with delay, falling within the scope of the speech. Inna and its noun; (أيها) is a vocative of the intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda); (الضالون) is a badal (substitute) of (أيها); and (المكذبون) is an adjective of (الضالون).
(لَآكِلُونَ مِنْ شَجَرٍ مِنْ زَقُّومٍ): the shifted lām; (آكلون) is the predicate of (إنكم); (من شجر) is attached to (آكلون); (من زقوم) is a badal of His words (من شجر), or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), or an adjective.
(فَمالِؤُنَ مِنْهَا الْبُطُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (مالئون) is conjoined to (آكلون); (منها) is attached to (مالئون); (البطون) is the object of the active participle. The pronoun referring to (الشجر) is feminine because it is a generic noun, and a generic noun may be treated as masculine or feminine.
(فَشارِبُونَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْحَمِيمِ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (شاربون) is conjoined to (آكلون); (عليه) is attached to an omitted ḥāl; (من الحميم) is attached to (شاربون).
(فَشارِبُونَ شُرْبَ الْهِيمِ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (شاربون) is conjoined to what preceded; (شرب الهيم) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). Conjoining a thing to itself is valid because the two are in reality different: the first is drinking boiling water as it is, at its extreme heat and cutting the bowels, which is a wondrous thing in itself; the second is drinking boiling water in that state as thirsty camels drink water, which is more wondrous and stranger still. In this simile there are two benefits: one, drawing attention to their drinking of it; the second, the futility of the drinking, and that what is drunk has no effect on it [i.e. the thirst], just as it has no effect on the thirsty camels.
(هذا نُزُلُهُمْ يَوْمَ الدِّينِ): (هذا) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (نزلهم) the predicate; (يوم الدين): the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. being on that grievous day.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words (لا بارد ولا كريم) there is the device of iḥtirās (guarding against misunderstanding), whose definition has preceded. Here, when He said (وظل من يحموم), it might be imagined that the shade could bring them some rest after weariness; so He negated of it the two attributes of shade, meaning: it is shade, but not like other shades that spread coolness and refreshment and bring benefit to whoever takes refuge in it and rests beneath it — in order to efface what the word "shade" connotes of finding relief in it. So His words (لا بارد ولا كريم) are two adjectives of (ظل), not of His words (من يحموم). Here an objection arises that the fāʾ conveys sequence with immediacy; we say that al-Raḍī stated explicitly that this is not obligatory [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse contains no fāʾ at this point, and the objection as printed appears defective], besides which, here it would lead to the imbalance of the two verse endings, and making them two adjectives of (يحموم) would not suit the Quranic eloquence. There is also in it the device of taʿrīḍ (innuendo): those who deserve the shade in which there is coolness and honour are other than these, which is more choking to their throats and more provocative of their regret. For all these subtle points, He gave the reason for their deserving this punishment by His words (إنهم كانوا قبل ذلك مترفين). Al-Rāzī said: "The wisdom in His mentioning the cause of their punishment, while not mentioning in the case of the Companions of the Right the cause of their reward — He did not say 'they were before that thankful and submissive' — is to draw attention to the fact that reward from Him, the Exalted, is grace, and punishment from Him is justice. Grace, whether its cause is mentioned or not, does not suggest any deficiency or injustice in the one who bestows it; but as for justice, if the cause of the punishment is not mentioned, it may be thought that He is unjust. This is shown by the fact that He, the Exalted, did not say regarding the Companions of the Right (جزاء بما كانوا يعملون) as He said regarding the forerunners, because the Companions of the Right were saved by the tremendous grace, not by deeds — unlike one whose good deeds are many, for whom the use of [the word] 'recompense' is fitting." This is very fine speech, so ponder it. And do not forget the hidden contrast (muqābala) latent between the lines of this wondrous speech: these who have come to this condition used to live in this world immersed in luxury, rolling about in its folds; and then, enveloped by scorching wind and black smoke, they remember what they used to be in and contrast it with their present state, with the embodiment and imagery present and ready before them, their hands feeling them by touch, in the manner of the saying of al-Buḥturī. [Translator's note: the source does not quote al-Buḥturī's verse here.]
2- In the verse (هذا نزلهم يوم الدين) there is the device of tahakkum (sarcasm), which has also passed: He called Hell and the kinds of torment and varieties of horrors in it "nuzul" (hospitality) in sarcasm at them, since nuzul is what is prepared for the guest to honour him — as in the words of the Exalted (فبشّرهم بعذاب أليم) — and like the saying of Abū al-Shaʿrāʾ al-Ḍabbī:
وكنّا إذا الجبار بالجيش ضافنا ... جعلنا القنا والمرهفات له نزلا
(Whenever a tyrant came to us as a guest with his army, we made the spears and the keen blades his hospitality.)
I.e. when the tyrant came down upon us with his army as a guest comes down. In it there is sarcasm at him, since he came to make war; so he likened him to one who came seeking kindness, and reinforced (rashshaḥa) that simile by making the spears and the keen, sharpened swords his nuzul, which is the food prepared for the guest.

dervis-irab:57-74.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تُمْنُونَ): "amnā yumnī" and "manā yamnī": to emit semen (al-maniyy) into the womb, i.e. the sperm-drop (nuṭfa). Ibn al-Sammāk read "tamnūn" with fatḥa on the tāʾ. The origin is from al-many, which is measuring out (taqdīr). The poet said:
لا تأمنّ وإن أمسيت في حرم ... حتى تلاقي ما يمني لك الماني
(Do not feel secure, even if you find yourself in a sanctuary, until you meet what the Measurer has measured out for you.)
From it comes al-maniyya (death), because it is measured out and comes according to a measure. In al-Mukhtār: "manā, of the pattern ramā, and also amnā."
(قَدَّرْنا): with the doubled and the single [dāl]. [The poet] said:
ومفرهة عنس قدرت لساقها ... فخرت كما تتايع الريح بالقفل
(And many a strong she-camel, mother of fine young — I measured [my blow] for her shank, and she fell, as the wind tosses dry branches about.)
The meaning is: I measured my blow for her shank, struck her, and she fell. Similar in meaning is:
وإن تعتذر بالمحلّ من ذي ضروعها ... على الضيف يجرح في عراقيبها نصلي
(And if she excuses herself from the guest by the drought of her udders, my blade wounds her hamstrings.)
(حُطاماً): al-ḥuṭām is dry, broken stalks of no use as food or nourishment; the root meaning of al-ḥaṭm is breaking. Al-ḥuṭam is the one who drives [the camels] violently, crushing them against one another. [The poet] said:
قد لفّها الليل بسواق حطم ... ليس براعي إبل ولا غنم
ولا بجزار على ظهر وضم
(The night has wrapped them up with a rough, crushing driver — no herder of camels or sheep, nor a butcher at the chopping-block.)
(تَفَكَّهُونَ): al-tafakkuh originally means partaking of various kinds of fruit (fawākih) to eat. Al-fukāha is jesting; from it is the ḥadīth of Zayd: "He was among the most jesting of people with his family." "Rajul fakih": good-humoured. It has been borrowed here for moving from one topic of talk to another. It is also said that its meaning is "you regret", its literal sense being "you cast jest away from yourselves", and jest is cast away only through grief; so it is of the type of taḥarraja and taʾaththama [i.e. tafaʿʿala of privation]. It is also said that (تفكهون) means you wonder; it is said you blame one another; and it is said you lament. All of that is explaining by what is entailed (al-tafsīr bi-l-lāzim).
(لَمُغْرَمُونَ): plural of mughram; the mughram is the one whose wealth has gone without compensation. The root meaning of this group is clinging, and al-gharām is the clinging punishment. Al-Aʿshā said:
إن يعاقب يكن غراما وإن يع ... ط جزيلا فإنه لا يبالي
(If he punishes, it is a lasting torment; and if he gives abundantly, he does not care [how much].)
(تُورُونَ): al-īrāʾ is making fire appear by striking. One says "awrā yūrī", and "warīyat bika zinādī", i.e. my affair has been lit up through you. One says "qadaḥa fa-awrā" when the fire appears; when it does not produce fire one says "qadaḥa fa-akbā". In al-Miṣbāḥ: "warā al-zandu yarī wariyan, of the pattern waʿā; in a dialect, wariya yarī with kasra on both; and awrā with the alif — that is when it brings out its fire." In al-Mukhtār: "awrāhu ghayruhu: someone else brought out its fire." In the dictionaries: you extract fire from al-zinād, plural of zand. The zand is the stick with which fire is struck, the upper one; the zanda is the lower one, which has a hole in it and is the female. When the two come together they are called zandān, and the plural is zinād. The Arabs strike fire with two sticks, rubbing one against the other.
(الْمُزْنِ): clouds; plural of muzna. In al-Qāmūs: "al-muzn, with ḍamma, is clouds, or the white of them, or the ones bearing water; the piece is a muzna."
(أُجاجاً): in al-Mukhtār: "māʾ ujāj: bitter water, intensely salty. Ajja al-māʾu yaʾujju ujūjan, with ḍamma."
(لِلْمُقْوِينَ): for travellers, i.e. We made it something that travellers benefit from. They were singled out for mention because their benefit from it is greater than that of residents. Quṭrub said: "al-muqwī is one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād): the poor man is called muqwī because he is empty of wealth, and the rich man is called muqwī because of his power (quwwa) to obtain what he wants." It is also said that al-muqwī is the one who alights in al-qawāʾ, the land where there is no one; "aqwat al-dār": the abode became empty of its people. Al-Nābigha said:
أقوى وأقفر من نعم وغيّرها ... هوج الرياح بهابي الترب موار
(It has become empty and deserted of Nuʿm, and the reckless winds have changed it with swirling fine dust.)
ʿAntara said:
حييت من طلل تقادم عهده ... أقوى وأقفر بعد أم الهيثم
(Greetings to you, O ruin whose time has grown long; it has become empty and deserted after Umm al-Haytham.)

* I'rab:
(نَحْنُ خَلَقْناكُمْ فَلَوْلا تُصَدِّقُونَ): (نحن) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause (خلقناكم) the khabar (predicate); the fāʾ is a conjunction; (لولا) is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); (تصدقون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent).
(أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ ما تُمْنُونَ): the hamza is for the disapproving interrogative; the fāʾ is conjunctive; (رأيتم) is a past verb and its agent, and its meaning is "tell me"; (ما) is a relative noun meaning "alladhī" (that which), the first object of (رأيتم); and the clause (تمنون) is the ṣila (relative clause).
(أَأَنْتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُ أَمْ نَحْنُ الْخالِقُونَ): the interrogative clause is in the place of the second object of (رأيتم). (أنتم) is a subject and the clause (تخلقونه) its predicate. (أنتم) may also be parsed as the agent of an implied verb, i.e. "do you create it?"; when the verb was omitted because what follows indicates it, the pronoun became detached. This is of the category of ishtighāl (preoccupation), and perhaps, in terms of the rules, it is more sound because of the interrogative particle. (أم) is a conjunction; it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), because a clause follows it, and the disconnected one is construed as "bal" (rather) plus the interrogative hamza. So the speech contains two questions: the first, "Do you create it?", whose answer is no; and the second, taken from (أم), i.e. "Rather, are We the creators?", whose answer is yes. (أم) may also be connected (muttaṣila), in which case it is correlative (muʿādila). This view is supported by the fact that the speech amounts to "which of the two things is the case?", and the clause after it is interpreted as a single word. (نحن) is a subject and (الخالقون) a predicate.
(نَحْنُ قَدَّرْنا بَيْنَكُمُ الْمَوْتَ وَما نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ): (نحن) is a subject and the clause (قدرنا) its predicate; (قدرنا) is a verb and its agent; the adverb is attached to (قدرنا); (الموت) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. We made it obligatory and decreed it for you. The wāw is conjunctive or parenthetical; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negating (ما), and (نحن) its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (مسبوقين) is genitive in form and accusative in position, because it is the predicate of (ما).
(عَلى أَنْ نُبَدِّلَ أَمْثالَكُمْ وَنُنْشِئَكُمْ فِي ما لا تَعْلَمُونَ): (على) is a preposition, and (أن نبدل) is in the interpretation of a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in the genitive by (على); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (مسبوقين), i.e. no one can outstrip Us in Our replacing your likes. They may also be attached to (قدّرنا بينكم), i.e. We have decreed death among you on [the basis] that We replace [you] — i.e. some people die and other people succeed them — in which case the clause (وما نحن بمسبوقين) is parenthetical. (ننشئكم) is conjoined to (نبدل); (فيما) is attached to (ننشئكم), and the clause (لا تعلمون) is the ṣila, i.e. We bring you into being in forms you do not know, of debased animals that wallow in filth, like apes and swine.
(وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ النَّشْأَةَ الْأُولى فَلَوْلا تَذَكَّرُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; the lām is the answer to the omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of verification; (علمتم) is a verb and its agent; (النشأة) is a direct object and (الأولى) a naʿt (adjective). (فلولا): the fāʾ is conjunctive, (لولا) a particle of urging, and (تذكرون) an imperfect verb and its agent.
(أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ ما تَحْرُثُونَ أَأَنْتُمْ تَزْرَعُونَهُ أَمْ نَحْنُ الزَّارِعُونَ): the i'rab of its parallel has preceded, so refresh your memory of it.
(لَوْ نَشاءُ لَجَعَلْناهُ حُطاماً فَظَلْتُمْ تَفَكَّهُونَ): (لو) is conditional; (نشاء) is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "naḥnu" (We); the lām occurs in the answer of (لو); (جعلناه) is a verb, its agent and a direct object; (حطاما) is the second object of (جعل); and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (ظلتم) is an incomplete past verb; its origin is "ẓaliltum" with kasra on the lām, the middle radical having been dropped for lightness; the tāʾ is its noun, and the clause (تفكهون) its predicate; (تفكهون) is an imperfect verb from which one of its two tāʾs has been dropped.
(إِنَّا لَمُغْرَمُونَ): inna and its noun, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and (مغرمون) its predicate. The clause of (إنّ), its noun and its predicate is the speech quoted by an omitted verb of saying, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied form being "so you would remain lamenting, saying" — or "you would say" — "(إنّا لمغرمون)", i.e. we are made to bear the loss of what we spent, or we are ruined by the ruin of our provision.
(بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ): (بل) is a particle of turning away (iḍrāb) and conjunction; (نحن) is a subject and (محرومون) a predicate; the clause is conjoined to the one before it.
(أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ الْماءَ الَّذِي تَشْرَبُونَ، أَأَنْتُمْ أَنْزَلْتُمُوهُ مِنَ الْمُزْنِ أَمْ نَحْنُ الْمُنْزِلُونَ): the i'rab of its parallel has preceded; (الذي) is an adjective of (الماء), the clause (تشربون) is the ṣila, and the referent pronoun is omitted.
(لَوْ نَشاءُ جَعَلْناهُ أُجاجاً فَلَوْلا تَشْكُرُونَ): its i'rab has preceded. The secret of omitting the lām in this verse and mentioning it in the first verse will come in the Rhetoric section.
(أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ النَّارَ الَّتِي تُورُونَ أَأَنْتُمْ أَنْشَأْتُمْ شَجَرَتَها أَمْ نَحْنُ الْمُنْشِؤُنَ): the i'rab of its parallel has preceded.
(نَحْنُ جَعَلْناها تَذْكِرَةً وَمَتاعاً لِلْمُقْوِينَ): (نحن) is a subject and the clause (جعلناها) its predicate; (تذكرة) is the second object; (متاعا) is conjoined to (تذكرة); (للمقوين) is attached to (متاعا) or is an adjective of it.
(فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (implying an unstated condition), i.e. if you have come to know these benefits and dazzling favours, then glorify. (سبّح) is an imperative verb and its agent is "anta" (you); (باسم) is attached to (سبّح) or to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. seeking blessing. It is also said that (اسم) is inserted (muqḥam). (العظيم) is an adjective of (ربك).

* Rhetoric:
1- In the aforementioned verses there is the device of ṣiḥḥat al-aqsām (exhaustive division), which has been mentioned before in this book: it consists of the speaker covering all the divisions of the meaning he is dealing with, so that he leaves nothing of it out. He turned from the word of deprivation and withholding to a word that is its consequent (ridf) and follows it, namely the word "jaʿl" (making), when He said (أفرأيتم ما تحرثون أأنتم تزرعونه أم نحن الزارعون لو نشاء لجعلناه حطاما). Likewise the word of reckoning [the favour] of water came, where He said (لو نشاء جعلناه أجاجا), with the word "jaʿl" when mentioning deprivation and what has its meaning; while giving came with the word "zarʿ" (sowing) regarding tillage, and with the word "inzāl" (sending down) regarding water. If it is said: why did He emphasise the verb with the lām in His words about the crop (لو نشاء لجعلناه حطاما), and not emphasise it about the water, where He said (لَوْ نَشاءُ جَعَلْناهُ أُجاجاً)? I say: because the crop — its growth, and its drying after freshness until it becomes broken stalks — might be imagined to be the doing of the farmers; that is why He, glory be to Him, said (أأنتم تزرعونه أم نحن الزارعون). Or it might be imagined that its fertility comes from watering, and its drying from the heat of the sun and lack of watering, or the repeated passing of whirlwinds. So He, glory be to Him, informed that He is in reality the doer of all that, and that He is able, if He willed, to make it broken stalks in the state of its growth and the time of its youth and freshness. Since this false impression was possible, eloquence required emphasising the verb of making in it and attributing it to its true Sower and Originator, in order to remove this impression. And since sending down water from the sky is impossible [for creatures], such that no possibility enters of anyone imagining that anyone of all creation is able to do it, there was no need to emphasise the verb in making it bitter; for no one could imagine that anyone sends down water from the sky bitter — nor sweet, which is easier and simpler than the first.
Al-Zamakhsharī's wording on this matter is as follows: "If you say: why was the lām brought into the answer of (لو) in His words (لجعلناه حطاما) and removed from it here? I say: since (لو) enters upon two clauses, the second of which is dependent on the first as the requital is dependent on the condition, and it is not purely conditional like (إن), nor does it govern as it does — the conditional meaning has only pervaded it incidentally, inasmuch as it conveys, regarding the contents of its two clauses, that the second was precluded because the first was precluded — it needed, in its answer, something set up as a sign of this dependency; so this lām was added to be a sign of that. If it is omitted after it has become a well-known sign in its place, that is because when a thing is known and its place is well known, and it has become familiar and customary, one does not mind dropping it from the wording, relying on the hearer's knowledge. Do you not see what is related of Ruʾba, that he used to say 'khayrin' to whoever said to him 'How are you this morning?' — he dropped the preposition because everyone knew its place, and its omission and its presence were alike since the matter was well known. And sufficient for you is the saying of Aws:
حتى إذا الكلّاب قال لها ... كاليوم مطلوبا ولا طلبا"
(Until, when the hound-master said to her: [never have I seen] the like of today for a quarry, nor for a pursuit.)
I say: in the verse of Aws ibn Ḥajar — or of al-Namir ibn Tawlab — there is an omission without which it is not sound, i.e. "he said to her: I have not seen the like of today for a quarry". The pronoun is for the hunting bitch, and al-kallāb is the trainer of the dogs, or the hunter; i.e. the quarry and the pursuit on this day are not like them on another day, but greater. Then al-Zamakhsharī continues: "It may also be said that this lām undoubtedly conveys the meaning of emphasis, so it was brought into the verse about food rather than the verse about drink, to indicate that the matter of food takes precedence over the matter of drink, and that the threat of losing it is more severe and harder, since drink is needed only as a consequence of food. Do you not see that you give your guest to drink only after you have fed him? Were you to reverse it, you would fall under the saying of Abū al-ʿAlāʾ:
إذا سقيت ضيوف الناس محضا ... سقوا أضيافهم شبما زلالا
(When people's guests are given pure milk to drink, they give their guests cold, limpid water to drink.)
One of the Arabs was given a drink and said: 'I drink only on top of a thamīla.' That is why the verse about food was put before the verse about drink." Al-thamīla is pure milk. [Translator's note: so in the source; al-Zamakhsharī's point concerns drinking only after food, and lexicons commonly gloss thamīla as what remains of food in the stomach.]
We return to the verse of Abū al-ʿAlāʾ and say: it is from an ode in which he praised Saʿd al-Dawla Abū al-Faḍāʾil. He was faulted because he praised [them] for giving guests water before mentioning food. Al-makhḍ is milk whose butter has been removed, so it has the meaning of mamkhūḍ (churned); it is also narrated "maḥḍan" with the undotted ḥāʾ, i.e. pure, sweet or sour. Al-shabim is cold, and al-zulāl is sweet [water]. [Translator's note: the verse as quoted above has «محضا» with ḥāʾ, while the explanation treats «مخض» with khāʾ as the primary reading.]
Moreover, since the scholars of rhetoric have given the context (maqām) a role in indicating what is meant, we say that the meaning of the verse is: when people hasten milk to their guests and content themselves with it instead of hastening food, they [the praised ones] hasten food, because of their preparedness for guests; so [the guests] need to drink water, and they give them water to drink before others have fed their guests. So their giving water conveys, with the help of the context, that food was hastened before it, because water customarily follows it; so there is no fault in it.
2- In these verses there is also the device of tashīm (anticipation), which is that the earlier part of the speech indicates what comes later, or the reverse. So in His words (أفرأيتم ما تحرثون) up to His words (أفرأيتم النار التي تورون), the beginnings of these verses require that their endings [Translator's note: the source sentence is defective here, «تقتضي أوائل هذه الآيات أن أواخرها»; evidently «تقتضي أوائل هذه الآيات أواخرها» (the beginnings require the endings)] — a verbal and semantic requirement — just as the words in them harmonise with their neighbouring meanings, the fitting with the fitting and the suitable with the suitable; because the mention of tillage suits the mention of sowing, and the reckoning [of the favour] that He, glory be to Him, did not make it broken stalks suits their being able to enjoy it. On this verse the arrangement of its sister [verses] is to be measured.
